title: Updating My Grading Policy Because You're All Using AI All The Time
author: Dan Meyer
summary: Dan Meyer writes his new grading policy as a mock legal resolution, with a series of WHEREAS clauses and BE IT RESOLVED terms. The premises are that students use AI constantly on homework, that this raises completion but lowers assessment scores, and that students know it harms their learning. He describes a prisoner's dilemma in which each student weighs honest work against AI output for a better grade, and a poisonous arms race of AI detection and evasion between teachers and students. His response is to make in-class, AI-free exams worth 80 percent of the grade and to grade homework only as complete or incomplete. Students may use AI however they like on homework, and a pasted-in LLM answer still earns credit. Students decide where they want his feedback, so his effort goes where their own developing skill and taste are invested, and attaching prompts is encouraged.
points: Meyer starts from the observation that AI use raises homework completion while lowering assessment scores, which he equates with less learning.
He frames student AI use as a prisoner's dilemma driven by finite admissions, grades on a curve and jobs.
The teacher-student relationship has become an arms race of detection tools and evasion tools, which he calls poisonous.
His policy weights in-class exams without AI at 80 percent and grades homework only as complete or incomplete.
Students choose where they want feedback, because feedback on LLM output helps neither side, and are invited to attach prompts.
quotes: WHEREAS, student AI use results in greater homework completion but lower assessment scores a/k/a less learning;
WHEREAS, students are in a prisoner’s dilemma with one another, each one competing for finite college admissions, finite grades on a curve, finite jobs,
WHEREAS, this relationship between teachers and students is really quite poisonous, with both sides locked in an arms race
BE IT RESOLVED, exams will count for 80% of your final grade. These will be taken in-class and without the assistance of AI;
If you copy and paste the assignment into an LLM and turn in the result, you will receive a score of “complete,” no questions asked;
Neither of us benefit when I give your LLM feedback. Both of us benefit when you help me invest my energy in the places where you have invested your developing knowledge, skill, and taste.
WHEREAS, we can both be grown-ups here and admit that students are using AI all the time to complete their homework;
